name: The Neuroscience School: Short Courses for High School Students
org: Georgia State University, Center for Behavioral Neuroscience
what_you_do: Take a one-week summer neuroscience course taught by Georgia State professors. Choices include a Boot Camp, fruit fly lab courses on Alzheimer's or stress, and advanced topics. Some run in person, some online.
who_can_apply: High school students who have completed 9th, 10th, 11th, or 12th grade before class starts. In-person courses also require you to be at least 16 by the start of class, with no exceptions.
pay_detail: Costs $275 to $350 per course in 2026. Fee help is available if you qualify for free or reduced lunch (documentation required). Email NeuroscienceSchool@gsu.edu.
duration: 4 or 5 days per course. In person 9:30 AM to 3:45 PM, online 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM. 2026 courses ran June 1 to July 23.
deadline_text: In 2026, registration stayed open until classes were full, and classes without enough sign-ups by June 1 were canceled. The 2026 schedule was posted in December 2025. 2027 courses are not posted.
how_to_apply: Register and pay in the GSU Marketplace Mall store linked from the Registration page. No essay or application.
notes: Online courses are open to younger high schoolers who are under 16. Sign up for the program's newsletter on the home page to hear when the 2027 schedule is posted.
